newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late weather-related gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late weather-related gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held decent gains late Tuesday in moderate trade, driven by forecasts for colder weather next week for the eastern half of the nation, industry sources said.
At 1420 EST, March rallied 17.7 cents to $2.49 per million British thermal units, while April was 15.3 cents higher at $2.26. Most others were up by three to 10.8 cents.

"I think it got a little overdone to the downside, then the colder six to ten day forecast triggered the rally," said one Houston-based trader, adding short covering after the recent down move also helped prop up the complex.

Traders said forecasts next week for much-below normal Midwest weather coupled with normal to below-normal expectations for the East and South helped stem the recent slide. But most agreed only protracted Arctic cold could fuel much higher numbers, particularly with eastern storage comfortable and likely to get more so in the next two weeks.
Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report range from 150-180 bcf compared to a 213 bcf decline in the same week last year.
Technically, traders pegged March resistance at $2.50 and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area. Trendline support was seen in the $2.30 area and then at the November 5 low of $2.12.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were 10 cents higher in the mid-to-high $2.50s. Midcon pipes also were up a dime to the low-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 21,230 Hub contracts traded by 1355 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1200 EST.
On the KCBT, March climbed 14 cents to $2.195, while April was still seven cents higher at $1.925. The East/West spread widened by 3.7 cents to 29.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
